adaptations.hook: What evidence belongs on a candidate-guideline review card?

content.title: Discuss a hypothetical review queue
content.body: The synthetic concept proposes a draft guideline after an example change. A pending-review queue would keep acceptance, revision and rejection explicit. Which evidence would help distinguish a reusable guideline from one unusual change?
content.closing_question: What would you review before accepting such a candidate?

adaptations.hook: A fictional review card turns one change into a question.

content.subject: A draft guideline needs a review decision
content.preview: A synthetic concept separates a proposal from an active rule.
content.body: The invented review sketch puts candidate guidelines in a pending-review queue. Its proposed next step is a review decision, rather than automatic activation. This is a controlled concept example; it does not establish audience interest or effectiveness.
content.call_to_action: Reply with the evidence you would want on a review card.

adaptations.hook: Picture a draft guideline waiting for a review decision.

content.spoken_opening: Could this example change suggest a guideline worth reviewing?
content.visual_concept: Show an invented change, then a candidate card entering a pending-review column. Display accept, revise and reject options. Keep a synthetic concept label visible and leave the card unapproved.
content.call_to_action: Which evidence would you inspect first?

assumptions.claim: Some readers might want to discuss candidate-guideline review cards.
assumptions.reason: Audience interest and usefulness have not been measured; this is synthetic test material.
